title: Karna's abandonment
hook: asked who his father is, Karna has no royal answer; Duryodhana makes him a king, and an old charioteer walks into the arena
carry: it follows him into every room

segments.voice: Yesterday, Karna matched Arjuna, and Kunti knew her son and kept silent. She can't tell anyone.

Two fighters are ready to face each other. Then Kripa, one of the teachers, steps between them with a question that sounds polite. Arjuna is a prince, son of Pandu and Kunti. Tell us your mother and father, your royal line. A prince fights only an equal. And Karna, who has just matched every feat in the arena, has no answer to give. The text says he lowers his face.
screen: `KRIPA ASKS FOR HIS LINEAGE.` → `A PRINCE FIGHTS ONLY AN EQUAL.` → `KARNA LOWERS HIS FACE.`

segments.voice: Duryodhana jumps in. If Arjuna will only fight a king, then let Karna be a king. And there in the arena he has Karna crowned king of Anga. Karna, overwhelmed, asks what he can give in return. Duryodhana asks only for his friendship, and Karna gives it. Then, through the crowd, comes an old man, trembling, his cloth slipping. It's Adhiratha, the charioteer who pulled a basket from the river. And Karna, the new king, his hair still wet from the crowning, bows his head to him and greets him as his father. Adhiratha holds him and weeps. It's the moment Bhima has been waiting for. You're a charioteer's son, he says, so pick up a whip; you're not fit to fight Arjuna, or to rule Anga. Duryodhana defends his friend: the origins of heroes, like the sources of rivers, are hard to know. Look at the armor and earrings this man was born with. Then the sun sets, and the day ends with nothing settled. Look at these six days together: a girl's curiosity, a basket, a charioteer's home, an armor given away, a mother's silent recognition, and now a crown and an insult on the same afternoon. Karna's abandonment isn't one event. It follows him into every room. And the thing held against him, his birth, is the one thing he doesn't know the truth of.
screen: `DURYODHANA CROWNS HIM KING OF ANGA.` · `KARNA BOWS TO ADHIRATHA.` · `BHIMA: PICK UP A WHIP.` · `LIKE RIVERS, HARD TO TRACE.` · then, large: `IT FOLLOWS HIM INTO EVERY ROOM.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a time someone asked where you're from, or who your people are, and the question landed hard, or a time you asked it of someone. Then think of one thing you've done that you're glad of, and let both sit side by side, the question and the deed.
Karna's abandonment. Asked his lineage, he lowers his face; crowned king, he bows to a charioteer; and the secret of his birth goes on following him.
Your line: it follows him into every room. Next, a house built for the Pandavas. Day seven hundred thirty-three, done.

howItsDone: In retellings, Karna's bow to Adhiratha in the arena is told as a sign of his loyalty to the father who raised him, and his friendship with Duryodhana is traced to this day.

original.note: Sanskrit sūta: a charioteer; Bhima throws the word at Karna as an insult.

trapdoor: what you thought: Karna is made a king and the matter's settled.
what it means: the crown answers Kripa's question, but Bhima's insult shows the question of birth isn't going away.

what a scholar hears: Duryodhana points to the armor and earrings as signs of a high birth, and the listener knows he is more right than he can know; the fight itself never happens, because the sun sets.

chat.says: Why did Duryodhana make Karna a king right there in the arena?
options: So Arjuna couldn't refuse to fight him for not being royal.
Because Kripa revealed that Karna was secretly a prince of Anga.
As a reward for Karna giving his armor to Duryodhana's teacher.
chat.meaning: Kripa said a prince fights only an equal. Duryodhana answered by crowning Karna king of Anga on the spot, asking only friendship in return.

Adhiratha.meaning: the charioteer who found the basket and raised Karna

Bhima.meaning: Pandu's second son, the strong one, son of Vayu

recall: the pale prince who was crowned
